title: Finite purely inseparable constant and variable root construction
statement: Let k→K be fields in one universe [def-pc-field-extension], s a finite subset algebraically independent over k [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], p prime with char(k)=p, and C a finite subset of k. There exist compatible extensions k→l→L and k→K→L with l/k and L/K finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], a finite subset t of L independent over l, and a compatible embedding k(s)→l(t). Each c∈C has a p-th root in l, each generator x∈s mapped to l(t) has a p-th root in l(t), and K together with l(t) generates L.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 04KM, coefficient-root construction in the induction step

proof.text: In the algebraic closure Ω of K, choose the unique p-th root rt(z) of each z. Let U be the finite image of C under c ↦ rt(c), and V the finite image of s under x ↦ rt(x). Define actual intermediate fields l=k(U) and L=K(U∪V) in Ω. These types have the same universe as K.

Each generator has its p-th power in the appropriate base field. Apply IntermediateField.isPurelyInseparable_adjoin_iff_pow_mem with exponent 1 to prove l/k and L/K purely inseparable. The generators satisfy the monic polynomials X^p-c. Apply the finite algebraic-generators lemma to U and U∪V to prove both extensions finite.

The generators of l lie in L, so adjoin_le_iff gives l⊆L. Define the algebra l→L by this inclusion; its composite with L→Ω is the original inclusion. For x∈s let r(x) be rt(x) as an element of L and define t as its finite range. The equations r(x)^p=x hold by the root construction.

Map the independence of s from K to Ω. Since l/k is finite and therefore algebraic, apply AlgebraicIndependent.extendScalars to obtain independence of the images of s over l. Frobenius on Ω sends the tuple r to those images. Naturality of Frobenius and injectivity of Frobenius on l allow AlgebraicIndependent.of_ringHom_of_comp_eq to deduce independence of r over l. Passing to its range gives independence of t.

Write E=k(s), E₁=l(t). Every image of an element of s is r(x)^p and hence belongs to E₁. Induction on membership in the adjoin, with cases generators, constants, addition, inverse and multiplication, proves the image of every element of E lies in E₁. Restrict the canonical ring homomorphism E→L to E₁ to obtain the asserted algebra and tower. Constants in C have roots in l and the original generators have roots in E₁ by construction.

Let B be the intermediate field in L generated over E₁ by the range of K→L. Induct on membership in L=K(U∪V). Constant roots belong to l and hence E₁; variable roots belong to t and hence E₁; images of K belong to B by definition. Addition, inverse and multiplication preserve B. Thus every element of L lies in B, giving B=top.

theorem exists_finiteRooted_extension
    (k K : Type w) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (s : Finset K) (hs : AlgebraicIndependent k ((↑) : s → K))
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (C : Finset k) :
    ∃ (l : Type w) (_hl : Field l) (_akl : Algebra k l)
      (L : Type w) (_hL : Field L) (_aKL : Algebra K L) (_alL : Algebra l L)
      (_akL : Algebra k L) (_htl : IsScalarTower k l L) (_htK : IsScalarTower k K L),
      Module.Finite k l ∧ IsPurelyInseparable k l ∧
      Module.Finite K L ∧ IsPurelyInseparable K L ∧
      ∃ t : Finset L, AlgebraicIndependent l ((↑) : t → L) ∧
        ∃ (_a : Algebra (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
            (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L))),
          IsScalarTower (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
            (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L)) L ∧
          (∀ c ∈ C, ∃ b : l, algebraMap k l c = b ^ p) ∧
          (∀ x (hx : x ∈ s), ∃ b : IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L),
            algebraMap (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
              (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L))
              ⟨x, IntermediateField.subset_adjoin k (s : Set K) hx⟩ = b ^ p) ∧
          IntermediateField.adjoin (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L))
            (Set.range (algebraMap K L)) = ⊤
